blocks.content: HEALTHCHECK tells Docker how to actively test whether a container is actually working, not just whether its process happens to still be running.

A process can be running while the application inside it is completely broken, deadlocked, out of memory, unable to reach its database. HEALTHCHECK defines a real test (usually a command that succeeds or fails) Docker runs periodically to check actual health, not just process existence.

blocks.alt: A real functional test, not just "is the process alive"

blocks.content: A container with a defined health check moves through its own small state machine: starting while the first checks have not yet run, healthy once checks are passing, and unhealthy if enough consecutive checks fail.

blocks.alt: starting, then healthy or unhealthy based on real checks

blocks.content: 3. Why This Matters Beyond a Single Container
blocks.text: 3. Why This Matters Beyond a Single Container

blocks.content: Health status is not just informational, orchestration tools and load balancers can read it and route traffic only to containers reporting healthy, automatically pulling a genuinely broken container out of rotation even while its process is technically still alive.

blocks.alt: Real infrastructure decisions get made from this status

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: HEALTHCHECK defines an actual functional test Docker runs periodically, not just a check that the process exists.
The resulting healthy/unhealthy status is used by orchestrators and load balancers to route traffic away from genuinely broken containers.
